name: Free Body Load Transfer Mechanisms Expanded
goal: Expanded re-run of the free-body load-transfer question, broadened to immersed-boundary, fictitious-domain, cut-cell, lattice-Boltzmann-IB and DEM-CFD formulations where they supply directly transferable force-transfer algorithms. Ranked by whether the mechanism is documented well enough to IMPLEMENT (discrete equations, force and torque accumulation rules, boundary or neighbour construction, sign conventions, time integration, pseudocode), with genuinely free six-DOF bodies ranked higher and 2021-onward GPU/differentiable MPM prioritized.
summary: The implementable literature separates into surface-load evaluation (pressure/stress integration or equivalent particle-boundary summation) and constraint-reaction methods that transfer an explicitly accumulated impulse or Lagrange-multiplier force, with free-body stability depending on treating the reaction AND ITS TORQUE consistently [Aki12, Kal14b, Glo01, Gio14]. SPH gives the clearest particle analogue: boundary particles generate pairwise pressure/contact forces whose equal-and-opposite fluid reaction is summed on the body [Aki12, Ban18b, Win20]. Eulerian variants integrate pressure and viscous traction, use moving-control-volume momentum balance when surface stresses are noisy [Nan17, Goz16b], or take conservative flux forces and torques at cut interfaces [Sch13b, Pus15]. Direct-forcing IB, fictitious-domain and LBM methods impose rigid velocity through delta-spread forces, distributed multipliers, penalty forces or link-wise momentum exchange, and the body update uses the NEGATIVE ACCUMULATED force/impulse and moment [Tai09, Tsc18b, Bha19, Wen15b]. These, rather than a bare mass-weighted grid-velocity average, define a physical reaction. VELOCITY EQUILIBRATION WITHOUT A SEPARATE IMPULSE ACCUMULATOR IS EXPLICITLY IDENTIFIED AS NONPHYSICAL FOR UNRESOLVED BODIES [Hyd19]. APIC supplies the MPM transfer principle, conservation of linear and angular momentum across particle-grid transfers [Jia16]; CPIC and interface-quadrature MPM extend it to solid-fluid interfaces [Hu18, Fan20]. Genuinely free six-DOF MPM implementations remain comparatively SPARSE [Li23e, Pro23b]. TOP-RANKED: Aki12, Tak20, Gis19b, Nan17, Tsc18b, Aan18.
